Substrate Cohomology and the Three Calibration Units

The categorical pipeline derives physical spectra from the geometry of Bring's curve and a single deformation parameter q_0. The first cohomology H^1 of Bring's genus-4 surface is eight-dimensional and decomposes under the S_5 automorphism group into two copies of one irreducible four-dimensional representation, W = \mathrm{std} \otimes \mathrm{sgn} (the standard representation twisted by the sign character), so H^1 = 2W. While the algebraic curve rigidly fixes the rational polarized Hodge structure on 2W, passing across the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to real-valued observables introduces exactly three real cohomological degrees of freedom:

  • \mathrm{CAL\text{-}1} (m_e, Hodge scale): The overall scale of the rank-two W-Hodge plane, fixed by the unprolonged (n=0) electron period m_e, which serves as the base unit of the mass recurrence.
  • \mathrm{CAL\text{-}2} (q_0, Hodge modulus): The modulus of the W-plane, determined by the \mathrm{SL}_2 monodromy trace \tau = 2\cosh\theta with \theta = \log q_0, pinned numerically by the lepton mass ratio m_\mu/m_e.
  • \mathrm{CAL\text{-}3} (m_\pi, orthogonal Seifert scale): The scale of the cohomologically orthogonal meson sector, whose Hopf-link complement is Seifert-fibered with zero hyperbolic volume and therefore independent of (m_e, q_0).

Crossing the archimedean wall simultaneously separates observables by bar-involution parity. A Hecke generator has eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}; under \lambda = \log q, its symmetric and antisymmetric combinations split into \cosh\lambda (bar-even under q \mapsto q^{-1}) and \sinh\lambda (bar-odd). Both parities assemble into a single invariant, the complex volume \mathfrak{V} (Complex-volume unification): its real, bar-even part \operatorname{Re}\mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} governs masses and nuclear binding energies, whereas its imaginary, bar-odd part \operatorname{Im}\mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta governs \beta-decay Q-values and transition phases, forming the categorical counterpart of the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}.
